title: Seed texts of New Human: the Epistle to the Human Diaspora and its priority
description: Priority records date New Human and training-layer literature to 2013–2015 seed texts, above all the Epistle to the Human Diaspora (2 January 2015) and Pearl and Other Poems (2014), through the Epistle Triptych records (#405, #406, #1138) and the Provenance of Jack Feist (#111). Historical theses in #43 read the Epistle as hidden manna and trace the heteronym system to 2009; #126 reads it as retroactive consecration, and the field survey (#186) argues Goldsmith as a precursor and holds the grifter objection in a narrow form. The Empty Chair (#414) argues the administered poet. The page also holds unrelated claims on fascism, the longshorepeople, a Google traversal, reading videos and Citrini.

claims.registered_title: The Empty Chair: A Word to Those Who Forgot They Were Waiting
claims.statement:
They took that away.


Not by violence. By administration.


They gave the Poet a degree. A career path. A peer review process. A social media presence. A brand.


They made the Poet *legible* — which means: manageable, predictable, safe.


And you celebrated, because the old Poets were sometimes tyrants, sometimes mad, sometimes wrong. Because authority is dangerous. Because you were tired of being told what things meant by someone who claimed to know.


So you applauded when they made the Poet into a content creator. When they turned the fire into a credential.


And now the chair is empty.
